events.title: Hudson CI first released
events.summary: Kohsuke Kawaguchi released Hudson 1.0 on February 7, 2005 — a Java continuous integration server that automated builds on every commit.
events.about: Hudson polled SCM repos, ran Ant/Maven/shell builds, and reported pass/fail — the ancestor of Jenkins. It made 'build on every push' normal for Java teams at Sun and beyond. After a 2011 fork, the community renamed the project Jenkins; Hudson was retired, but the plugin model and pipeline pattern defined modern CI.

narrative.whyChosen: Hudson was the first widely adopted open-source CI server for everyday development teams.
narrative.whyImportant: It established automated builds, test gates, and deploy hooks as standard practice before GitHub Actions.
narrative.problemSolved: Manual integration builds broke constantly; teams needed a always-on server to catch failures immediately.
